claims.text: Machine-learning methods, including neural networks, can predict thermodynamic properties of multicomponent high-entropy materials in high-temperature states.
Machine-learning methods would improve transition-temperature determination relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
Machine-learning methods would improve fusion-enthalpy determination relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
Machine-learning methods would improve fusion-entropy determination relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
Machine-learning methods would improve volume-change determination relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
Machine-learning methods would improve dense-fluid heat-capacity determination relative to existing experimental and computational methods.
Thermodynamic behavior in high-entropy alloys has relationships with composition and temperature.
Machine-learning models can learn the complex composition-temperature-thermodynamic-property relationships relevant to the solid-to-fluid transition.
Learning those relationships would produce accurate predictions of transition temperature, fusion properties, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity.
Improved computational predictions could support high-temperature alloy design and optimization.
The performance of the proposed method depends on the quality and quantity of its training data.
The performance of the proposed method depends on the selected machine-learning algorithm and model architecture.
The proposed hypothesis is scoped to multicomponent high-entropy materials at high temperatures and across varying compositions and temperatures.
